integrity: The proof reduces the homogeneous finite magnitude to a trapezoidal sum, computes the needed endpoint derivatives of the round distance profile, and applies Euler–Maclaurin through fourth order. The intrinsic endpoint is derived from exact geometric series. A standalone standard-library checker replays independent finite-sum and asymptotic consistency tests; finite tests are not used as an infinite proof.
scientific_limitations: The smooth asymptotic fixes circumference and relative curvature below the intrinsic endpoint before increasing the number of equally spaced samples. The intrinsic endpoint is treated separately by exact finite sums. No optimality claim is made among arbitrary point samples.
title: Curvature-universal sampling law for round-circle magnitude
